original_question: Does the family cwk(X) of all nonempty convex weakly compact subsets of a Banach space X have property (SC), meaning that one can choose a selector on cwk(X) whose composition with every scalarly measurable multifunction into cwk(X) is scalarly measurable?
target_in_paper: Section 2.3, Problem 2.9 (Fremlin): the open problem asking whether cwk(X) has property (SC).
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact target very closely. It identifies the right family, cwk(X), as the non-empty convex weakly compact subsets of X, and it correctly paraphrases property (SC) as the existence of a single selector on cwk(X) whose composition with every scalarly measurable cwk(X)-valued multifunction is scalarly measurable. It also stays on Problem 2.9 itself, rather than drifting to the neighboring Problem 2.8 about wk(X) or Problem 2.7 about existence of selectors for a single multifunction.
missing_details: The paper fixes a complete probability space (Omega, Sigma, mu) as the domain of the multifunctions in this subsection.
The ambient spaces are real Banach spaces, by the paper's global convention.
A set selector must be stated explicitly as a map psi:cwk(X)->X satisfying psi(C) in C for every C in cwk(X).

In this section, a multifunction F:Omega->P0(X) is 'scalarly measurable' in the precise sense that F^{-}(H)={t in Omega : F(t) intersects H is nonempty} belongs to Sigma for every open half-space H subset X.

The conclusion that psi composed with F is scalarly measurable concerns an X-valued function; explicitly, x* o psi o F must be measurable for every x* in X*, equivalently psi o F is Ba(X,w)-measurable.
The quantifier is uniform: one single selector psi must work simultaneously for every scalarly measurable multifunction F:Omega->cwk(X).
refined_question: Let (Omega, Sigma, mu) be a complete probability space and let X be a real Banach space. Write cwk(X) for the family of all non-empty convex weakly compact subsets of X. Does cwk(X) have property (SC), i.e. does there exist a set selector psi:cwk(X)->X with psi(C) in C for every C in cwk(X) such that, for every scalarly measurable multifunction F:Omega->cwk(X) (meaning F^{-}(H) in Sigma for every open half-space H subset X), the X-valued function psi o F:Omega->X is scalarly measurable?
justification: The paper states this essentially verbatim as Problem 2.9 in the measurable-selectors subsection. The draft is already paper-faithful; the only additions needed to make it fully stand-alone are the subsection's fixed measurable-space setup, the exact selector definition, the paper's precise meaning of scalar measurability for multifunctions, and the global convention that Banach spaces are real. I have not broadened the question to the larger family wk(X) or to the neighboring selector-existence question for a single multifunction.
